findings.text: the refusal case asserts only that the exit status is nonzero, so main() mutated to wrap parse_args as `except SystemExit: raise SystemExit()` -- a bare exit whose process status is 0, which is the success status the finding was about -- still reports 1 passed (hole_exit_none.log), and main() mutated to raise SystemExit(1) also reports 1 passed (hole_exit_one.log), so a failure ending in any generic nonzero is indistinguishable from the unproducible-tier refusal; pinning the specific code argparse yields (`assert refusal.value.code == 2`) closes both.

the hour case's expected values are computed from the table it should hold the entry point to -- window_seconds = TIER_WINDOW_SECONDS[tier] feeds the expected row count at 466, the expected endpoint series at 467 and the expected declared weight at 471 -- so changing TIER_HOUR from 3600 to 1800 leaves the hour case green (control_window_hour_1800.log: 1 failed, 2 passed, the failure being the record case at 539), meaning the case that exists to pin the entry point's window moves with the thing it checks; writing the two windows out literally in the parametrisation (minute 60 s / 3 samples, hour 3600 s / 180 samples) would redden.
